title: VPC upgrade orchestrator and health-probe strategy for zero-downtime runtime rollouts
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Background: Private (VPC) customers run Redwood's data plane inside their networks, which requires a carefully orchestrated runtime upgrade process to avoid dropped requests, KV-cache inconsistencies, and operator intervention. Goal: implement an upgrade orchestrator (operator + IaC hooks) and a probe-driven canary rollout algorithm that achieves near-zero downtime and deterministic automated rollback on safety signals.

Scope: Terraform module changes to expose orchestration knobs, an upgrade operator running in the control plane that executes coordinated node rotations, a probe library (gRPC + HTTP) for application-level readiness/health checks, pre-upgrade validation, staged canary policy, and a runbook + integration tests for private customers.

Non-goals: database schema migrations (handled separately), storage volume data migrations, long-lived model weight transfers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules expose 'orchestrator_enabled', 'canary_ratio_schedule', and 'max_concurrent_reboots' flags and are backward compatible
Operator implements probe-driven rollout: schedule steps 0%,1%,5%,25%,100% with gated metrics at each step
Automated rollback triggered if error-rate > 0.5% over 5m or P95 latency regression > 30% compared to baseline
No customer API errors or significant latency spikes observed in staging during 10 full upgrade rehearsals
Runbook created and linked in ticket; SRE and Solutions Engineering sign-off obtained
updates: 2026-03-02: Ticket created by Marcus Chen with initial requirements from PM and SRE; referenced customer outage post-upgrade.

2026-03-04: Design review with Sofia, Liam O'Connor (SRE), and Priya Nair (PM). Agreed on probe types: liveness (process), readiness (request path + KV warm-up), and semantic health (sample inference correctness).
2026-03-07: Prototype health-probe implemented: grpc.health + /internal/ready with KV-warm cache percentage metric. Initial PR: github.com/redwood-private/upgrade-operator/pull/11

2026-03-10: Terraform change proposal: add module outputs for orchestrator k8s role, taint labels, and canary config. Backwards compatible by default (orchestrator_enabled=false). Draft PR created github.com/redwood-ops/terraform-modules/pull/42

2026-03-12: Ran automated canary in staging cluster; discovered KV-cache warm-up takes up to 90s causing transient 5xx on heavy request bursts. Decided to add 'cold-start-protect' step: shadow traffic to new instance to populate KV before accepting production traffic.

2026-03-14: Implemented rollback marker artifacts retention: operator will keep prior image + config for 72h and publish rollback URL to console. Preparing runbook and scheduling 10 rehearsal upgrades next week.
runbook: Preflight: verify cluster health, circuit-breakers, and baseline latency for 30m
Step 1: enable orchestrator in Terraform (orchestrator_enabled=true) and apply (plan reviewed by SRE)
Step 2: operator creates canary set and starts at 1% traffic; wait for gate 5m
Step 3: ramp to 5% then 25% with automated gating checks at each step
If gate fails: operator marks rollout as FAILED, triggers automatic rollback to previous image, and creates incident in PagerDuty
Post-upgrade: validate KV cache hit-rate, tracing spans, and perform synthetic end-to-end test suites
testing_plan: Unit tests for probe library and operator state machine
Integration tests: local k3s + terraform modules to validate module outputs and RBAC changes
Staging rehearsals: 10 progressive upgrades with injected failures (network loss, pod eviction, slow-boot)
Chaos tests: randomized node reboots during canary window to validate operator resilience
Performance validation: measure P50/P95 token latency across rollout steps
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive canary ramp reduces total upgrade time but increases blast radius. Default schedule tuned conservatively for enterprise private customers.
Decision: operator will prefer in-place rolling restarts with node pinning over recreating entire pools to avoid IP drift in customer VPCs.
Terraform consideration: stateful resources (load balancer target groups, NAT) must be modified with minimal diffs; use lifecycle.ignore_changes for certain attributes.
Open question: whether to include a 'traffic-shadow' mode in console for manual verification — PM to prioritize based on customer signals.
